title: Explain OAuth2 to a newbie
ideal_answer:
OAuth2 lets an app act on your behalf without ever seeing your password.

The flow, simplified:
1. App redirects you to the provider (Google, GitHub, etc.) to log in
2. You approve the permissions it's asking for
3. Provider sends you back to the app with a temporary code
4. App swaps that code for an **access token** (server-to-server, hidden from you)
5. App uses the token to call APIs on your behalf

The token is scoped (only certain permissions) and expires. That's the whole point — limited, revocable access instead of handing over credentials.

Start with the **Authorization Code flow** — it's the standard for web apps and the one most tutorials assume.
prompt: Can you explain how OAuth2 works? I'm new to it and just want to understand the basic flow.
